Historical definition changes are documented in the A2 table below.

Cancer diagnosis confirmation | Require at least one HL-coded encounter | Incidental coding and data errors inflate apparent HL prevalence | Two separate encounters with a diagnosis of the same cancer type at least seven days apart required; applies to all cancer types | Prevents incidental code from driving cohort inclusion | 2026-05-29 | Cohort construction; cancer summary table

Insurance harmonization â€” same-day hierarchy | Apply payer hierarchy within a day when multiple tiers present | Multiple payer records on a single day with differing tiers | Hierarchy: Medicaid (incl. codes 93/14/FLM source) > Medicare > Private (incl. Tricare) > Other > Self-pay or Uninsured â†’ Uninsured > All missing â†’ missing | Deterministic resolution per guidance from Amy | 2026-05-01 | All payer-stratified analyses

ADI â€” ZIP9 extrapolation from matching encounter | Require ZIP9 for ADI; no fallback defined | Some encounters have only ZIP5 or no ZIP | If 5-digit ZIP in one encounter matches 9-digit ZIP in another encounter for the same patient, extrapolate 9-digit to 5-digit encounter | Team confirmed ZIPs consistent longitudinally | 2026-08-18 | ADI covariate assignment

ADI â€” population-weighted average for ZIP5-only | â€” | Encounters with only ZIP5 have no direct ZIP9 | Use population-weighted average ADI of the 5-digit ZIP when no 9-digit is available | Accepted standard for ZIP5-level ADI approximation | 2026-08-25 | ADI covariate assignment

RUCA â€” ZIP5 acceptable | Require ZIP9 for RUCA lookup | RUCA works natively at ZIP code level | Can use 5-digit ZIP for RUCA assignment | RUCA database supports 5-digit ZIP directly | 2026-08-25 | Rurality covariate

Relapse vs refractory definition | Single category: refractory/relapse HL | Clinically and analytically distinct | Relapse = change in tx regimen with break of 90+ days from end of initial tx; Refractory = change in regimen with break of fewer than 90 days | Two separate concepts clinically | 2026-09-11 | Episode classification; survival analyses

NHL-only episode exclusion | Include all patients with any HL code | Patients with multiple clearly NHL-only tx lines contaminate HL cohort | Patients whose multiple lines of tx are clearly NHL-only are removed from the dataset | Ensure cohort specificity for HL study | 2026-09-22 | Cohort; all analyses

Uncertain HL inclusion | Exclude borderline HL/NHL patients | Ambiguous HL/NHL classification in data | Err on side of including patients who may not be a true HL if information is not definite | Conservative inclusion reduces false exclusions | 2026-09-22 | Cohort

Distance cutoff â€” far from care binary | Binary distance variable with unresolved cutoff | Uncertainty about evidence-based cutoff | 100 miles, based on doi.org/10.1182/blood-2023-182477 | Published literature reference for HL care distance threshold | 2026-10-13 | Far-from-care analyses

Drug name normalization â€” brand to generic | Use raw drug names from source tables | Brand-name proliferation impedes regimen identification | Convert all brand names to generic equivalents (e.g., adriamycin to doxorubicin); includes liposomal variants | Consistency for regimen detection and reporting | 2026-10-13 | Chemo classification; regimen identification; all outputs

operations.insert_text: Expected Structure: Patients have encounters from one or more contributing SOURCE values. The pipeline produces two binary flags: `single_source_care` (all non-blank encounters came from a single institution) and `single_source_care_post` (the same rule applied to post-treatment encounters only). A `primary_source` column records the most frequent non-blank SOURCE value, with alphabetical tiebreaking.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Cleaning Rule â€” blank SOURCE exclusion: SOURCE values are normalized using NULLIF(UPPER(TRIM(SOURCE)), '') before any flag computation; blank SOURCE entries are excluded from the single-source determination.
Cleaning Rule â€” NA assignment: `single_source_care` is NA where `n_encounters` equals zero; `single_source_care_post` is NA where `n_encounters_post` equals zero.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: Chemotherapy hits are drawn from three PCORnet medication tables â€” PRESCRIBING, DISPENSING, and MED_ADMIN â€” via the `get_chemo_hits()` helper. Each returned row carries the patient ID, treatment date, triggering code, and a `source` column identifying the originating table path ("PRESCRIBING", "DISPENSING (NDC)", "MED_ADMIN (RX)", or "MED_ADMIN (NDC)").

Observed Issue â€” RXNORM_CUI mismatch: DISPENSING and MED_ADMIN rows in the Mailhot V1 extract lacked usable RXNORM_CUI values for direct RxNorm matching. Without a crosswalk, chemo hits from these two tables were silently dropped (Phase 122 SUMMARY).

Cleaning Rule â€” NDC-to-RxNorm crosswalk: An NDC-to-RxNorm crosswalk (`data/reference/ndc_rxnorm_crosswalk.rds`, built by `R/108_build_ndc_rxnorm_crosswalk.R`) is loaded and passed to `get_chemo_hits()`. For DISPENSING and MED_ADMIN NDC-path rows, `normalize_ndc()` strips hyphens from the raw NDC before lookup.
Cleaning Rule â€” graceful degradation: If the crosswalk is NULL or empty, the NDC-path DISPENSING and MED_ADMIN branches log a message and return zero rows rather than erroring.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: Drug names from all three medication tables are normalized to canonical generic equivalents before regimen detection. Normalization is applied to `MEDICATION_LOOKUP` values at config load time so that all downstream code receives pre-normalized names.

Observed Issue â€” brand-name proliferation: Brand names and salt variants (adriamycin, adriamycin pfs, adriamycin rdf; vinblastine sulfate) appear across medication tables. Without normalization these aliases produce distinct drug-name values that fail regimen detection logic.

Cleaning Rule â€” brand-to-generic mapping: `canonicalize_drug_name()` maps brand and salt variants to generic equivalents. Examples: adriamycin â†’ Doxorubicin; vinblastine sulfate â†’ Vinblastine; liposomal doxorubicin variants included. Applied to all MEDICATION_LOOKUP values on config load (DEC-011 CONFIRMED 2026-10-13).

Cleaning Rule â€” JCODE supplement: J-code entries (`MEDICATION_LOOKUP_JCODE_SUPPLEMENT`) are merged into `MEDICATION_LOOKUP` after canonicalization so that HCPCS J-codes resolve to the same generic names as RxNorm-derived entries.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: Treatment episodes are assigned a regimen label (ABVD, BV+AVD, Nivo+AVD, or unlabeled) based on the drug combination detected within the episode. Drug-name detection takes priority over J-code detection.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]
Cleaning Rule â€” ABVD labeling: An episode is labeled ABVD when it contains doxorubicin + bleomycin + vinblastine + dacarbazine with no brentuximab or nivolumab and at most four unique drugs.

Cleaning Rule â€” BV+AVD labeling: An episode is labeled BV+AVD when it contains brentuximab + doxorubicin + vinblastine + dacarbazine without bleomycin or nivolumab, and the episode start is on or after 2019-01-01.

Cleaning Rule â€” Nivo+AVD labeling: An episode is labeled Nivo+AVD when it contains nivolumab + doxorubicin + vinblastine + dacarbazine without bleomycin, has exactly four unique drugs, and the episode start is on or after 2024-01-01.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: Chemotherapy dates are collapsed into contiguous treatment episodes using a gap threshold measured from episode start. Each episode has an episode start, episode stop, length in days, and list of drugs. Two window sizes are produced: a 90-day and a 180-day variant.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Cleaning Rule â€” episode segmentation: `assign_episode_ids()` starts a new episode when `treatment_date - episode_start >= gap_threshold`. The default gap threshold is 90 days (`R/00_config.R:GAP_THRESHOLD = 90`, L4054). A 180-day variant is produced in the same script with `gap_threshold = 180L`.

Cleaning Rule â€” distinct constructs: Episode segmentation (gap measured from episode start), relapse/refractory classification (90-day break from end of initial treatment line â€” DEC-007), and Gantt display window (90-day or 180-day export file) are three separate constructs. A decision about one does not govern the others.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: Per-patient anthracycline exposure is summarized as two dates: `last_dose_firstline_dt` (last anthracycline admin date within first-line episodes) and `last_dose_ever_dt` (last admin date across all episodes). These are used as the clock start for echo surveillance rate calculations.

Observed Issue â€” first_line column absence: The `first_line` column is absent from `treatment_episode_detail_180.rds`. When all `first_line` values are FALSE or NA, `last_dose_firstline_dt` is NA for that patient (D-08a).

Cleaning Rule â€” first-line dose: `last_anthracycline_dose()` filters rows where `first_line == TRUE` to derive `last_dose_firstline_dt`; rows with `first_line == FALSE` or NA are excluded from the first-line clock.
Cleaning Rule â€” ever dose: `last_dose_ever_dt` is the maximum admin_date across all episode rows regardless of first-line status.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: A complete blood count (CBC) event is defined as the co-occurrence of WBC (LOINC 6690-2), hemoglobin (LOINC 718-7), and platelet (LOINC 777-3) results for the same patient on the same date. This definition is specific to the distance-CBC association analysis; it is not applied to survivorship encounter classification.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Cleaning Rule â€” three-LOINC requirement: `build_cbc_events()` filters LAB_RESULT_CM to the three LOINC codes via SQL push-down, then retains only dates where all three codes are present for the same patient (ID Ã— date grouping).
Cleaning Rule â€” DuckDB push-down: LAB_RESULT_CM is large; the LOINC filter and ID filter are applied in SQL before results are returned to R to reduce memory use.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: Rurality is assigned at the encounter level using RUCA (USDA 2020 ZIP Code Data) joined on ZIP5. Four RUCA categories: Metropolitan (codes 1â€“3), Micropolitan (4â€“6), Small town (7â€“9), Rural (10), Not coded (99). Five-digit ZIP is acceptable for RUCA assignment (DEC-006).

Observed Issue â€” missing reference file: If the RUCA reference file (`data/reference/RUCA-codes-2020-zipcode.xlsx`) is absent, `ruca_code` and `ruca_category` are NA for all encounters; the script degrades gracefully with a message.
Cleaning Rule â€” ZIP5 join: RUCA lookup joins the encounter-level ZIP5 column using `left_join` on ZIP5 with `na_matches = "never"` to exclude NA ZIPs from the join.
Cleaning Rule â€” primary RUCA code: The USDA 2020 primary RUCA code (column `PrimaryRUCA`, sheet "RUCA 2020 ZIP Code Data") is used; the code is truncated to integer before category assignment.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: The Social Deprivation Index (SDI; Robert Graham Center) is assigned at the encounter level using ZIP5 as the geographic unit. SDI scores range 0â€“100. SDI is ZIP5-level only; no ZIP9 or census-tract granularity is used.

Observed Issue â€” missing or malformed reference file: If `data/reference/zip5_sdi_reference.csv` is absent or lacks the expected ZIP5/SDI_score columns, `sdi_score` is NA for all encounters; the script logs the available column names and continues.
Cleaning Rule â€” ZIP5 normalization and join: `normalize_zip5_raw()` is applied to the reference ZIP5 column before join; SDI is joined by ZIP5 with `na_matches = "never"`.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: Diagnosis codes indicating non-malignant conditions associated with rituximab or methotrexate use (autoimmune, inflammatory, hematologic) are flagged via prefix match against `DOI_CODE_MAP` (defined in `R/00_config.R`). Both ICD-10 and ICD-9 codes are handled.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Cleaning Rule â€” DX_TYPE gating: `is_doi_code()` matches ICD-9 codes only against numeric-leading DOI_CODE_MAP keys and ICD-10 codes only against alpha-leading keys. This prevents cross-version false matches. ICD-9 records with DX_TYPE == "SM" or missing DX_TYPE are excluded.
Cleaning Rule â€” 4-then-3-character prefix cascade: `classify_doi_codes()` tries the 4-character prefix first, then the 3-character prefix, to allow both specific and category-level matches.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: Patients with ICD-10 C81.x or ICD-9 201.x codes are classified as HL. Patients whose treatment episodes are clearly NHL-only are excluded from the cohort (DEC-009). Patients with ambiguous HL/NHL classification are retained (DEC-010).

Observed Issue â€” mixed HL/NHL codes: Many patients have diagnoses for both HL and NHL. Gantt-based episode detection is used to identify episodes that are clearly NHL-only, but the precise episode-level classification logic was not located in a single function.
Cleaning Rule â€” NHL-only exclusion: Patients whose multiple treatment lines are clearly NHL-only are removed from the dataset (DEC-009 CONFIRMED 2026-09-22).
Cleaning Rule â€” uncertain HL inclusion: Patients who cannot be definitively confirmed as NHL-only are retained in the cohort, erring on the side of inclusion (DEC-010 CONFIRMED 2026-09-22).
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

Expected Structure: Encounters occurring after the patient's resolved death date are identified and quantified. Post-death encounters are not removed from the encounter table; they are flagged via the `post_death_activity_days` column and the `death_flag` variable.

Observed Issue â€” post-death encounters present in data: Some patients have encounters recorded after their death date. Phase 29 (`R/29_first_line_and_death_analysis.R:L258â€“L259`) reports the patient count with post-death activity.

Cleaning Rule â€” post-death activity flag: `resolve_death_date()` computes `post_death_activity_days` as `pmax(0, last_observed - death_date_raw)`; the value is zero for patients with no post-death activity and for patients with no death record. `death_flag` takes five values: plausible, implausible_post_activity, conflicting_resolved, conflicting_unresolved, no_death_record.
[TEAM INPUT NEEDED]

operations.insert_text: Insurance missingness and unmapped categories: A non-trivial proportion of patient-days have unmapped or missing payer type (Self-pay, Other, Other govt). Payer-stratified analyses may be affected by differential missingness.

Distance measurement: Distance is computed as straight-line distance between ZIP-code centroids, not driving distance or travel time. ZIP centroid-based approximation may introduce measurement error, particularly in rural areas with large ZIP geographies.

ZIP imputation for ADI: Where a nine-digit ZIP is unavailable, the population-weighted average ADI of the five-digit ZIP is used (DEC-004). This approximation introduces measurement error in the ADI covariate for encounters without nine-digit ZIP records.
Death capture: Death dates come from the DEATH table in the PCORnet CDM extract; deaths occurring outside participating sites or not reported to the contributing institutions may not be captured.
